title: Recurrent Rossby-wave-pattern detection and recurrence metrics
scientific_basis: Röthlisberger et al. (2019), Journal of Climate, recurrent Rossby-wave metric R
Zimin et al. (2003), Monthly Weather Review, Hilbert-transform wave-packet envelope
Ali et al. (2021), Geophysical Research Letters, recurrent Rossby waves and spell persistence

required_additional_data.reason: The published zonal-wavenumber filter requires complete 0-360 degree longitude coverage; the earlier 30-120E ERA5 archive is insufficient.

canonical_r_metric.time_filter: 15-day centred running mean, used as the daily-data approximation to the published 14.25-day filter
canonical_r_metric.definition: Modulus of the analytic signal reconstructed from the positive wavenumber-4-15 Fourier coefficients

climatology.method: Calendar-day mean, standard deviation, 75th percentile and 90th percentile
climatology.high_r_definition: Sector-mean R at or above its calendar-day 90th percentile

rrwp_episode.primary_definition: At least 3 consecutive sector high-R days
metrics: integrated R excess above the calendar-day p90 threshold

supplementary_distinct_recurrence_metric.purpose: Reduce the risk that one stationary amplified system is interpreted as recurrence of distinct packets
supplementary_distinct_recurrence_metric.field: Instantaneous wavenumber-4-15 V250 envelope before time smoothing
supplementary_distinct_recurrence_metric.distinct_recurrence_flag: At least 2 envelope peaks and at least one high-R day in the analysis window
supplementary_distinct_recurrence_metric.status: Operational sensitivity diagnostic, not a replacement for the published R metric

event_windows.event: Cold-spell onset through event end; secondary

statistics.multiple_testing: Benjamini-Hochberg FDR within primary and secondary metric families
statistics.robust_group_result: FDR q < 0.05 and leave-one-winter-out sign stability >= 0.90

interpretation_cautions: R identifies recurrent or quasi-stationary synoptic-wave amplitude but does not identify ridge or trough phase over Bangladesh.
High R can occasionally arise from one stationary amplified system; distinct-envelope-peak counts are therefore reported as a sensitivity diagnostic.
Daily 00 UTC data approximate the original 6-hourly 14.25-day filter with a 15-day centred daily filter.
The R metric and Takaya-Nakamura wave-activity flux diagnose different properties and should be interpreted together.
Statistical association does not independently establish causality.
